findings.proposedIrEvidence: ir-rule:170e314ceb35e54072b7ddba.exceptions[0..9] link only to permission rules for §6.01(a)(1)-(3) and §6.01(b)(1)(X),(1)(Y),(1)(Z),(3),(4)(a),(4)(b),(4)(c)
findings.verifierReasoning: The proposed IR models §6.01(a) as a single PROHIBITION rule whose 'exceptions' array is the mechanism connecting the blanket ban to the carve-outs that lift it. The source's own chapeau text states unambiguously that 'the provisions of Section 6.01(a) hereof shall not apply to' all 33 numbered clauses in (b). The proposed IR's exceptions array covers only roughly 10 of these carve-outs (through clause (4)(c)) and never links the prohibition to the ~20+ separately-modeled PERMISSION rules for clauses (5) through (33) (e.g. ir-rule:4b390b44... for (5)(a), ir-rule:8f3b7f1b... for (18)(i), ir-rule:2142a4b8... for (31), ir-rule:c2602aec... for (33), etc.), even though those rules exist elsewhere in the same IR as standalone permission objects. A consumer that relies on the prohibition rule's exceptions array to enumerate what actually carves out of the ban (a natural and common way to query 'what is this prohibition subject to') would conclude that only a small fraction of the source's actual permitted-debt universe exists, materially understating available capacity/permitted categories. The rule's own sufficiency is marked PARTIAL, but that flag does not convey the scale of the gap (roughly 70% of statutory carve-outs unlinked).

findings.sourceEvidence: (18) (i) Indebtedness, Disqualified Stock or Preferred Stock of Restricted Parties that are not Guarantors at any one time outstanding not to exceed... (ii) Indebtedness of Restricted Parties that are not Guarantors in respect of any working capital facilities to the extent non-recourse to the Loan Parties
findings.proposedIrEvidence: ir-rule:8f3b7f1b6dec1c302dd1194e has conditions: [] and entityScope/entityScopeExcluded both []; ir-rule:220b9dd4e6b869b29d809805 captures only the 'non-recourse to Loan Parties' condition but not the 'not Guarantors' restriction; both marked sufficiency COMPLETE
findings.verifierReasoning: The defining eligibility test of this basket - that the debt be incurred by a Restricted Party that is NOT a Guarantor - is the entire reason this clause exists as a separate, narrower category from the general baskets available to all Restricted Parties. Omitting this restriction (via entityScopeExcluded or an explicit condition) while marking the rule COMPLETE means a consumer of the IR has no way to prevent a Guarantor from being modeled as eligible to use this $720mm/100%-EBITDA-or-non-recourse capacity, which the source text plainly reserves for non-Guarantors only. This is consistent with, and a concrete instance of, the deterministic signal flagging that no rule in the IR records any entity-scope restriction despite the source distinguishing at least six entity categories (Borrower, Restricted Subsidiary, Guarantor, non-Guarantor Restricted Subsidiary, Unrestricted Subsidiary, Loan Parties) that materially affect who may rely on which basket.

findings.sourceEvidence: Indebtedness incurred by any Restricted Party on behalf of, or Guarantees of Indebtedness of, any Joint Ventures; provided that the aggregate principal amount of such Indebtedness incurred pursuant to this Section 6.01(b)(27) and together with any outstanding Indebtedness under Section 6.01(b)(13) hereof incurred to Refinance Indebtedness initially incurred in reliance on this Section 6.01(b)(27), shall not exceed... the greater of (x) $360.0 million and (y) 50% of Consolidated EBITDA
findings.proposedIrEvidence: ir-rule:9e88c326f5775e5d2535f3a3.capacityExpression is a standalone MAX($360mm, 50%*EBITDA) with no dependsOn/SHARES_CAPACITY_WITH link to ir-rule:40a36af71a396edc636637b5 (the §6.01(b)(13) refinancing rule), and sufficiency is marked COMPLETE
findings.verifierReasoning: Unlike the analogous baskets at §6.01(b)(12)(b), (18) and (19) - each of which the proposed IR correctly models via a LEDGER_USAGE_REFERENCE/shared cap plus an explicit dependsOn to the (13) refinancing rule - the (27) basket is modeled as an unconditioned MAX ceiling with no aggregation against Refinancing Indebtedness incurred under (13) to refinance (27)-originated debt, despite the source imposing exactly that same 'together with' aggregation language for (27) as it does for (12)(b)/(18)/(19). Marking this rule COMPLETE while omitting the aggregation mechanic risks double-counting capacity if (13)-refinancing debt tracing to (27) is not separately tracked elsewhere.

findings.sourceEvidence: ...in an aggregate principal amount or liquidation preference up to 200% of the gross unutilized cash and Cash Equivalents...; ...the First Lien Leverage Ratio of the Initial Borrower for the Test Period would be no greater than 2.50:1.00
findings.proposedIrEvidence: the 200% figure appears only inside a diagnostic 'attemptedStructure' side-field of an UNSUPPORTED node (ir-rule:53287a6e), and the 2.50:1.00 figure appears only as prose inside a 'reason'/'semanticDescription' string (ir-rule:f77f334c), rather than as a structured, computable numeric literal in the operative capacityExpression tree
findings.verifierReasoning: The deterministic pass correctly observes that these source-stated numeric anchors (200%, 2.50x) are not present as usable PERCENT/RATIO values anywhere a downstream evaluator would consult. However, both host rules are already honestly marked UNSUPPORTED/PARTIAL for exactly the reason that these clauses require multi-step or inverse computations the compiler could not resolve, so this is a completeness/traceability gap in the disclosure rather than an affirmative misrepresentation of capacity - a future remediation pass should ensure these key figures are preserved as structured literals so they are not lost.
